earlier_scan.note: Attested only via Nachtigal wordlist (Lukas & Voelckers 1938); extinct, no phonology/stress description.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021 (draft). The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan. Cambridge: circulated draft.
sources.note: Nothing on Mimi-N. Sec. 2.3 (p.6) lists the three 'Mimi' sources (Decorse 1907, Lukas & Voelckers 1939, Jungraithmayr 1971) and calls Nachtigal's Mimi 'mysterious and still not clearly affiliated'; sec. 4.3 'Tones' concerns Maba and Aiki only; the word 'stress' does not occur.
sources.venue: The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan

sources.citation: Starostin, George. 2011. On Mimi. Journal of Language Relationship 6: 115-140.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative/lexicostatistical study of Mimi-N and Mimi-D vs Maban; reproduces Nachtigal's Mimi-N forms (via Lukas & Voelckers 1938), a few of which carry acute marks (e.g. imperatives z=áia 'come!', z=úlko 'leave!', p.~125), but never says what the marks denote; explicitly states that grammatical data are unknown for both Mimis (p.117). No occurrence of 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' in the text.

sources.citation: Greenberg, Joseph H. 1950. Studies in African Linguistic Classification: VII. Smaller Families; Index of Languages. Southwestern Journal of Anthropology 6(4): 388-398 (sec. 9 'Mimi (of Nachtigal)', pp. 388-389).
sources.note: No phonology content. States only that Nachtigal 'has given a brief account of the language of the Mimi', that it differs from Gaudefroy-Demombynes' Mimi, shows a few vocabulary resemblances to Maba possibly due to borrowing, and 'must be considered an independent family'. (Reprinted in Greenberg 1955; 1963/1966 reclassify it under Maban -- browse-only copies, same absence of phonology.)

Völckers, Nachtigals Aufzeichnungen über die Sprache der Mimi in Wadai (Bearbeitung eines Wörterverzeichnisses unter Heranziehung anderer Quellen)').
sources.note: No phonology content; one-line notice that characterizes Lukas & Völckers 1938 as an edition of a word list drawing on other sources -- i.e. confirms the Glottolog's most extensive description is a wordlist, not a sketch.

sources.citation: Wiktionary. Appendix: Mimi of Nachtigal word list (transcription of Lukas & Völckers 1938, Mimi-N to German and German to Mimi-N).
sources.note: Wordlist-only data: c. 25 of c. 110 forms carry an acute accent (álgun 'acht', áziṅki 'Stimme', búfuk, dérkē, fáila, fúla, káǰi, káran, kárik, kérim, kíndoi, kúńtik, kúrmudi, kúrši, kúyi, nína, ótu, ráikun, rákaba, sála, sáya, zíri!, zī́ka; non-initial: gelémfi, kanám, sarkái, tokíe, yáila, ǰā́u!), macrons mark length; no note says whether the acute is stress or pitch. Not a statement.

sources.citation: Nachtigal, Gustav. 1889. Saharâ und Sûdân: Ergebnisse sechsjähriger Reisen in Afrika. Dritter Theil: Wadâï und Dâr-Fôr. Leipzig: F. A. Brockhaus. (Book VII, tribes of Wadai: 'Die Mimi und ihr Bezirk')
sources.note: No phonology content. The only linguistic remark: 'Die Sprache der Mimi ist eine besondere, welche sich sowol von der der Abū [Araber] als von der Bora Mābang unterscheidet' (djvu text line ~8926) and that the Mimi 'stehen dieser [Māba-Gruppe] doch durchaus fern'. Nothing on accent, stress or tone; the vocabulary itself is not printed here (published posthumously by Lukas & Völckers 1938).

sources.note: The only primary publication of Mimi-N (Nachtigal's ca. 1870 notes, edited by Lukas). Nachtigal's forms carry acute marks; Lukas's editorial introduction is the one place a remark on what the accents denote (Ton/Akzent) could exist. 10 pages, German.

sources.note: Record only (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a wordlist, 9 pp; Starostin 2011:116 summarises it): publishes Jungraithmayr's brief 1959 Abeche fieldnotes on a third 'Mimi' (= Amdang) and compares them with the published Mimi-N (Nachtigal, via Lukas & Voelckers 1938) and Mimi-D lists, concluding the three are different languages; for Mimi-N it is second-hand lexical comparison only, and no tone or accent statement for Mimi-N is expected or was seen.
